rationale: Sertraline (SSRI; t½ ~26h; moderate discontinuation syndrome risk) to agomelatine (MT1/MT2 agonist, 5-HT2C antagonist; t½ ~2h). Sertraline has moderate discontinuation syndrome risk — taper over at least 2 weeks. Agomelatine can be started during the sertraline taper without serotonin syndrome risk. Sertraline is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor but agomelatine is metabolised by CYP1A2 (not CYP2D6) — no interaction. CRITICAL: Baseline LFTs before starting agomelatine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Continue sertraline 100 mg. CHECK BASELINE LFTs before starting agomelatine. No serotonin syndrome risk: agomelatine does not inhibit serotonin reuptake. Sertraline is a CYP2D6 inhibitor — no interaction with agomelatine (CYP1A2 substrate).
Reduce sertraline to 50 mg. Continue agomelatine 25 mg. Monitor for discontinuation symptoms at this reduction.
Stop sertraline. Continue agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Sertraline discontinuation is usually mild — dizziness, irritability. Titrate agomelatine to 50 mg at 2 weeks if inadequate response.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sertraline 100 mg → agomelatine 25 mg (standard dose range for MDD). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

contraindications: ALT >3× ULN at baseline — do not start agomelatine.
